note: HOST COST of the simulator, as opposed to the in-game results in bn1.json.
The unit is `vhPerWallMinute` -- virtual hours of game bought per real
minute of waiting. It improves UPWARD. Everything else the harness reports
is virtual time and says nothing about how long a run takes to sit through.
RULES.
1. Only move a number from a run you actually observed, and record the
machine: these are wall-clock measurements, so they are comparable
only against other measurements on the same hardware. A 5% gap is
noise; a 2x gap is a finding.
2. `decayPct` is the whole point of the entry. It compares the mean
per-interval throughput of the FIRST HALF of a bounded window's samples
against the SECOND HALF -- not the first sample against the last, which
is the two least reliable readings (JIT warm-up, and a partial tail).
Strongly negative means cost grows with run length, which is a different
bug from `vhPerWallMinute` simply being low, and the one this simulator
has historically actually had (see spec/simulator.md, 'Run-length
pathologies').
3. A budgeted run never reaches its goal. These entries are diagnostics
and are never route evidence.
HOW TO RE-MEASURE.
bun run sim -- --profile bn1-full --seed 1 --compact --perf \
--wall-budget 2m --cost
bun run sim:profile --cpu-prof --wall-budget 2m   # where the time goes
bun run sim:profile --matrix                      # which subsystem owns it
Same seed, same budget, an otherwise idle machine.

provenance.recordedFrom: first measurement, taken when --wall-budget and --cost were added

bn1-full.what: Cold BN1 start under the settings bench:sim:bn1-full uses.
bn1-full.note: THE PROBLEM, not a target. At a flat 2.89 vh/min the 24h horizon would take ~8 minutes a seed. It is not flat: throughput halves across the window and the last interval measured 1.02 vh/min and was still falling, so the run does not finish in any reasonable time. Fix the decay before the absolute number. Reproduced twice at this revision within 0.4%.

whereTheTimeGoes.note: Self+total time from a 2-minute `sim:profile --cpu-prof` at the same revision. The two chains are roughly equal and independent.
whereTheTimeGoes.hackingDispatch: 31.5% -- runPump -> pump -> planFarm -> dispatch. Inside it ramInvestment (game/lib/features/hacking.ts:968) is 15.0%, almost all of it marginalCostPerGb (shared/strategy/ram-supply.ts:143, 9.7%) sorting a supply list with compareSupply (4.6% self, entirely under native sort).
whereTheTimeGoes.targeting: 20.4% -- solveCycle (shared/strategy/targeting.ts:429) via stepEvaluator and solveEntry, spending it in evalThreads -> packsAt -> place. packsAt alone is 7.0% self.
whereTheTimeGoes.factionsPortfolio: 20.7% -- a 30-second-cadence feature taking a fifth of the CPU. factions tick -> stepFactions -> decideFactions -> selectFactionPortfolio -> chooseBudget -> evaluate (15.3%), of which evaluateUncached is 10.8%, so the memo misses most of the time. estimatedCost/greedyOrder (shared/strategy/factions/augs.ts:823) 8.8%.
